title: Maple Leaf management; society jobs and lawn parties
summary: He lists places like country clubs and private parties played, which paid a dollar and a half.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But who managed to Maple Leaf? I didn't get that. Oh, Gaspar.
He was the manager? Yeah, the bass player. And might as well say I was the manager because everything they had to consult with when we went to Shreveport. That's right.
And what other places did you play? Did you play La Louisiane ever?

For Mr. Fayette? Oh my goodness. Ask me how many times. Antoine, Louisiana, St. Charles, Grunewald, Jewish Country Club, New Orleans Country Club, all the children dancing in the yard and things like that for the rich people. Oh my goodness. You couldn't name a place there. I didn't play in New Orleans. Betsy Coles? You couldn't name one place.
I'm going to put you on the spot. What about Betsy Coles? Did you play her La Long Potties?
What's she called, Betsy Coles? La Long Potties.
She was up on Willow, I think.
I played all kinds of La Long Potties.
They didn't pay though. They didn't pay. No, they didn't? Oh no. Dollar and a half the most. That's right. Dollar and a half you got to play La Long Potties.
That sounds somewhat like the rich people paying for the weddings. They give the orchids a handkerchief, you see, like this. They spend five hundred dollars on flowers.
